idiom_name: thread_local! key, LocalKey::with / try_with, Cell/RefCell helpers
implementation_notes: Rust absorbs the pattern into the standard library: thread_local! declares a static key of type LocalKey<T>, the value is initialised lazily on first use in each thread and destroyed at thread exit, and the key uses the fastest TLS implementation available on the target platform. Because with() hands out a shared reference, mutable state needs interior mutability - Cell or RefCell, for which LocalKey<Cell<T>> and LocalKey<RefCell<T>> have dedicated helpers - and the const block initialiser avoids lazy-initialisation overhead. The classic key/collection/proxy structure is replaced by the macro and the key type. The classic form stays justified whenever the state really is thread-owned scratch data; for async tasks it is usually the wrong unit.
pitfalls: LocalKey::with panics when the key has already been destroyed (for example when called from a destructor), and the Cell/RefCell helpers panic on a re-entrant borrow_mut; try_with returns an AccessError instead of panicking, so destructors and callbacks should use it.
A thread-local destructor that panics aborts the whole process - the std documentation states this explicitly, so destructors must not propagate panics.
Values are per OS thread, not per task: all futures polled on one executor thread share the key, so async context needs tokio::task::LocalKey or an explicit parameter.
The initialiser runs once per thread even when the thread only touches the key incidentally, so keep it cheap or use const initialisation.

variants.name: tokio::task_local! (task-owned state for async runtimes)
variants.implementation_notes: When many tasks are polled on one executor thread, the unit that needs its own value is the task, and tokio::task_local! declares exactly that: the macro builds on a thread_local key internally, and LocalKey::scope(value, future) binds the value for the future and its nested futures, dropping it when the scope completes. Unlike the standard key, task-local values are not lazily initialised - with() panics when no value is bound - so scope the value before spawning work or use try_with. Choose it whenever request or trace context must follow an async task; keep the standard thread_local! for genuinely thread-owned scratch data.
pitfalls: Scope is not inheritance: tasks started with tokio::spawn begin a fresh task scope and do not see the value, so context must be re-bound or passed where it is spawned.
with() and get() panic when no value is bound for the current task; prefer try_with or a scope that always binds before spawning.
Polling a scoped future inside with()/try_with on the same key panics, and nesting the same key shadows the outer value rather than merging it.
